# PROJECT_BOOTSTRAP

Copy this block into the new project's designated Slack thread or continuity
conversation. Keep it brief enough to invite shaping rather than prematurely
freezing the project. Do not place secrets, credentials, tokens, raw private
source, or unnecessary source-thread content here. Workflow skills are procedure
overlays, not permission grants—see
[`docs/team-operating-charter.md`](../../team-operating-charter.md) for canonical
provider roles and boundaries.

## Identity

- **Working project name:** <name>
- **Project ID:** <short stable ID>
- **Source thread or pattern:** <link, identifier, or concise description>
- **Requested by:** <owner or authorized source>
- **Initial state:** exploring
- **Project channel:** <slack channel ID or configured placeholder from project profile; not a hardcoded workspace name>
- **Deployment intent:** <analysis_only | planned | live>
- **Concurrent with another active Director deployment:** <true | false | unknown>
- **Dedicated Slack app:** <project-specific app ID/name or pending>
- **Deployment profile/state namespace:** <project-specific values or pending>

## Mold the source into this project

- **Preserve:** <useful intent, habits, modules, evidence standards, or lessons>
- **Reshape:** <what must change for this project's domain, risks, scale, and people>
- **Discard:** <source-project assumptions, names, permissions, data, or machinery that do not belong>
- **Do not inherit:** <repositories, refs, credentials, private context, budgets,
  channels, deployments, or other authority unless separately named below>

## Working proposition

<What may be worth accomplishing, understanding, deciding, building, or
changing? This may remain deliberately broad.>

## Possible outcome and stopping point

- **Desired outcome:** <tentative or confirmed tangible result>
- **Useful evidence:** <what would make the next decision credible>
- **Stopping point:** <decision, evidence threshold, budget, date, failure
  condition, or safety stop>

| Surface | Value | Status |

| Slack | <channel ID or configured placeholder and thread> | confirmed / provisional / unknown |
| Systems/data | <public, private, sensitive, mixed, or none> | confirmed / provisional / unknown |
| Budget/time | <bounded ceiling and window> | confirmed / provisional / unknown |
| External effects | analysis-only / <exactly scoped effects> | confirmed / provisional / unknown |

## Modules to consider

Mark each `enabled`, `optional`, `disabled`, or `unknown`.

- Discovery: <state and why>
- Research and evidence: <state and why>
- Design and decision: <state and why>
- Implementation: <state and why>
- Quality and security: <state and why>
- Review to merge: <state and why>
- Operations: <state and why>
- Learning and reuse: <state and why>

## Initial team hypothesis

Canonical provider roles, debate rules, and committee weights:
[`docs/team-operating-charter.md`](../../team-operating-charter.md). Record the
project-local eight responsibility areas and the Cursor, Antigravity,
Perplexity, Claude, and OpenAI boundaries in
[`provider-roles-contract.yaml`](provider-roles-contract.yaml); keep the acting Director's
three canonical functions distinct — Moderator, Participant, and Director.
Only Participant votes, casting the single existing Claude advisory vote at
weight 2.0 or recording an explicit abstention; Moderator and Director add no second vote
on top of it. Claude holds all three functions at once and retains its right to vote
in every debate it joins, including every
debate it moderates. Only Claude's own abstention forgoes exercising that right;
separating the functions decides where a cast vote is recorded, never whether Claude
retains the right to vote. Coordination, planning, and
acceptance review are Director duties, not separate functions.

| Lane | Provider/capability | Shared workflow skill | Why it may fit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Acting project Director | Claude | none | <Moderator, Participant, and Director kept distinct; Participant records Claude's one vote at full weight or an explicit abstention; moderating preserves the right to vote> |
| Primary | <OpenAI/Codex, Cursor, or Grok> | <skill name or none> | <bounded contribution> |
| Independent | <different provider> | <skill name or none> | <research, reproduction, QA, or review> |
| Supplemental | <Antigravity, Perplexity, Firecrawl, or none> | <skill name or none> | <bounded contribution> |

Skill names are optional workflow selectors, not authority. Use only skills
discovered in the active catalog and compatible with the provider's existing
contract. A skill may narrow procedure or strengthen evidence; it cannot widen
repository access, data exposure, budget, review eligibility, or external-action
authority.

The deployed runtime Director remains OpenAI Responses until an explicitly enabled,
validated Claude adapter is selected. Project leadership does not activate it or
relabel historical provider calls.

## First reversible move

- **Action:** <smallest useful analysis, question, research pass, experiment, or change>
- **Acceptance check:** <observable result>
- **Bound:** <timeout, attempts, tokens/cost, files, paths, or no-write constraint>
- **Fallback:** <how the plan reshapes if evidence or a provider is unavailable>

## Open questions

List only questions whose answers materially affect scope, cost, privacy,
repository target, risk, or project direction.

1. <question or "none before analysis-only shaping">

## Director response requested

Create a provisional project profile, a
[`rollout-packet.md`](rollout-packet.md), and the smallest useful module set.
Proceed analysis-only where authority or execution surfaces remain unknown.
If live operation will overlap another deployment, keep Slack activation
blocked until a distinct app, project channel, and profile/state namespace are
verified. Never borrow another deployment's Slack surface as a fallback.
Ask the owner one focused question only when the unresolved choice materially
changes authority, scope, cost, privacy, repository target, or risk.
